title: AWS Reworks EventBridge Custom Buses for Enterprise-Scale Event-Driven Architectures
gist: AWS launched an enhanced EventBridge Custom Event Bus that can be shared across accounts via RAM with up to 10,000 subscribers, plus retention/replay up to 365 days, content-based dedup and ingress/egress pricing. It moves EventBridge toward enterprise event backbone territory without replacing Kafka.

insights.claim: The enhanced EventBridge Custom Event Bus can be shared across AWS accounts through AWS Resource Access Manager and supports up to 10,000 subscribers by default, replacing fragile cross-account rule and forwarding topologies.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: AWS is targeting enterprise multi-account event architectures, a sticky platform-lock-in lever.
insights.locator: The enhanced Custom Event Bus can be shared

insights.claim: The model shifts governance: a platform team sets boundaries on a central bus while application teams manage their own subscriptions, filtering, targets, retries and failure destinations, reducing onboarding work for new consumers.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Lower marginal cost of adding consumers increases usage and consumption of AWS event services.

insights.claim: A new Subscriber resource consolidates filtering, target configuration, retries and dead-letter destinations into one consumer definition and supports variable start times for onboarding and replay.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Simplifies operations and removes glue configuration, favoring staying within AWS.
insights.locator: The new Subscriber resource is another important change

themes.theme: Durability, delivery semantics and Kafka comparison

insights.claim: The bus retains events for 1 to 365 days, supports replay, JSONata transformations, and deserializes Avro and Protocol Buffers into JSON for filtering, making it a more durable backbone.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Retention and replay erode a key differentiator of streaming platforms for mid-scale use cases.
insights.locator: The bus itself also becomes more useful

insights.claim: Content-based deduplication collapses matching events within a five-minute window for exactly-once semantics in that scenario, but application-level idempotency is still required, especially for replays or cross-region processing.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Exactly-once claims are narrow; engineering risk persists.
insights.quote: This does not remove the need for application-level idempotency
insights.locator: The enhanced bus adds content-based deduplication

insights.claim: Synchronous invocation for targets such as AWS Lambda can eliminate the pattern of placing SQS between EventBridge and Lambda just to get stronger processing acknowledgement.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Fewer intermediate services may shift AWS spend away from SQS toward EventBridge.

insights.claim: EventBridge is moving into territory of enterprise brokers like Apache Kafka but remains a managed serverless router, not a direct replacement for Kafka in every high-throughput streaming architecture built on durable logs, partitions and consumer groups.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Managed Kafka and Confluent-type vendors face incremental, not wholesale, competitive pressure.
insights.locator: The enhanced EventBridge model moves into territory

insights.claim: Pricing moves to an ingress and egress throughput model, where publishers pay for events ingested and subscribers for events delivered, so cost no longer compounds with each cross-account or bus-to-bus forwarding hop.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Pricing now scales with data volume rather than topology, lowering cost for large fan-out architectures.
insights.locator: AWS has also changed the pricing model

insights.claim: Existing custom buses continue unchanged and are relabelled Custom event bus-classic, while the enhanced bus is a separate resource, available initially in selected regions in North America, Europe and Asia Pacific.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Incremental adoption lowers migration friction; limited regions delay broad uptake.
